NDT training on the Gulf Coast: how it works

Short answer: Gulf Coast technicians take NDT theory online through the Atlantis portal, self-paced, with an ASNT NDT Level III available for questions, then complete hands-on training and the practical examination at the employer's plant, yard or shop under a written practice based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. The contractor or plant that employs you issues the certification. Atlantis NDT has no classroom on the Gulf Coast; its Houston office is a business address, not a training site.

The arrangement matches how the corridor from Corpus Christi to Pascagoula fills its rosters. Inspection contractors staff up ahead of the spring and fall turnaround seasons, plants and shipyards hire through the year, and every one of them prefers a new technician who has finished the theory and can show documented hours. Course access opens as soon as you enrol, whatever the month, and the published US course fees on this page list Level I and Level II for UT, RT, MT, PT and VT. Atlantis's other office is in Hyderabad, India; national course detail is on NDT training in the USA.

Where NDT technicians work along the Gulf Coast

The Houston Ship Channel. Refineries, chemical plants and terminals line the channel through Houston, Pasadena, Deer Park and Baytown, where ExxonMobil runs one of the largest refining and petrochemical complexes in the country. The work is in-service examination for the plants' mechanical integrity programmes: ultrasonic thickness readings at condition monitoring locations, weld examination and repair verification during turnarounds, and tank and exchanger inspection. Many inspection contractors keep their main crew base in the Houston area for that reason.

Texas City, Freeport and Galveston Bay. Texas City holds Marathon's Galveston Bay refinery and other process plants on the bay; Freeport has Dow's Texas Operations and the Freeport LNG export terminal. Chemical plants run a wider range of alloys than refineries, including stainless steels, nickel alloys and clad vessels, which makes penetrant testing and material verification common alongside UT.

The Golden Triangle and the Sabine. Beaumont, Port Arthur and Orange form a dense refining cluster, with Motiva's Port Arthur refinery, the country's largest by capacity, and ExxonMobil's Beaumont refinery. LNG has reached the Sabine as well: Golden Pass near Sabine Pass produced its first LNG in 2026, and Sabine Pass LNG and Cameron LNG operate on the Louisiana side.

Lake Charles and southwest Louisiana. Lake Charles combines refining and chemicals in Calcasieu Parish with the LNG plants in Cameron Parish to the south, where new liquefaction trains keep construction examination busy. Construction NDT is a different job from plant maintenance: radiography and UT of new pipe welds, PT and VT on stainless cryogenic piping, and documentation against the construction code rather than an inspection plan.

Baton Rouge, the river parishes and New Orleans. ExxonMobil's Baton Rouge refinery and chemical plant anchor the upper end of the Mississippi River industrial corridor, which runs past dozens of chemical plants and several refineries down to New Orleans. Baton Rouge is also where many Louisiana contractors station their plant crews. To the south, Houma and the bayou yards build and repair offshore supply vessels and fabricate offshore structures.

Corpus Christi. Corpus Christi pairs refineries with crude export terminals on its ship channel and Cheniere's Corpus Christi LNG, which completed its Stage 3 expansion in 2026. Pipelines from the Permian Basin and the Eagle Ford end here, so integrity digs and pipeline construction join plant work.

Shipbuilding in Pascagoula and Mobile. HII's Ingalls Shipbuilding in Pascagoula builds amphibious ships, destroyers and Coast Guard cutters, and Austal USA builds Navy and Coast Guard vessels in Mobile, where Airbus also assembles commercial aircraft. Navy hulls bring NAVSEA requirements; the Chevron refinery in Pascagoula and the steel mill north of Mobile add plant work to a shipbuilding economy.

Which NDT methods and levels Gulf Coast employers ask for

Corridor contractors hire Level II technicians to run jobs and sign results, and Level I trainees to assist and log hours. Here is how the methods and governing documents line up by sector.

SectorMethods in demandCodes and documents that govern acceptance
Refinery and chemical plant maintenanceUT thickness, VT, PT, MT, RT; PAUT and TOFD on weldsAPI 510, API 570, ASME B31.3, ASME Section V, owner specifications
Storage tanks and terminalsUT, VT, MT, MFL floor scanningAPI 653, owner specifications
New construction and fabrication shopsVT, MT, PT, UT, RTASME Section VIII, ASME B31.3, AWS D1.1
LNG plantsRT, UT, PT, VTASME B31.3, API 620, API 625, owner specifications
Naval and commercial shipbuildingVT, MT, PT, UT, RTNAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, MIL-STD-2035, ABS rules
Offshore fabricationVT, MT, UTAWS D1.1, API RP 2X
PipelinesVT, RT, UTAPI 1104, 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195

Thickness gauging on piping circuits is the everyday job of corridor plant inspection and the usual entry point into UT; see ultrasonic testing training. Shipyards and fabrication shops lean on VT, MT and PT, which is where Level 1 training pays off quickly, and Level 2 training is what lets you interpret and report on your own. Plant inspectors certified by API under 510, 570 or 653 direct the inspection programme, while NDT technicians carry out the examinations; Atlantis offers self-paced online API 510, 570, 580 and 653 exam-prep courses for those moving into that role.

How NDT certification moves between Gulf Coast employers

Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Alabama do not license NDT technicians by method. Certification belongs to the employer: each contractor, plant or yard keeps a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A and certifies its own people against it. On the Gulf Coast those written practices are mostly written around in-service plant scope, which is why a UT Level II moving from one Houston contractor to another can usually recertify quickly, with new specific and practical examinations on the new company's procedures, a vision check and a records review rather than a fresh start.

Two layers sit on top of contractor certification here. Many operators qualify contractor technicians themselves before letting them work on site, often with a practical test on the operator's own samples for thickness or weld UT. Site access needs its own paperwork too: a TWIC card for maritime-regulated facilities, the plant's safety orientation and, for pipeline work, the operator qualification required under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. None of these is an NDT certification, and none replaces one. Shipyard work adds the NAVSEA personnel requirements, which the yard's own programme and Level III must satisfy.

ASNT central certification is the technician's own credential and does not lapse when you change contractors. At Level III, the ASNT certificate is the common basis employers use when they certify a Level III; our Level III preparation covers the ASNT Basic and method examinations. The SNT-TC-1A eligibility tool shows what each level asks of you, and companies whose written practice has drifted away from the work they actually do can use written practice development.

Radiography licensing in Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Alabama

All four Gulf states are NRC Agreement States and license industrial radiography themselves: Texas through the Department of State Health Services, Louisiana through the Department of Environmental Quality, Mississippi through the State Department of Health and Alabama through the Department of Public Health. Each state's rules require radiographers to be trained in radiation safety and certified before they work without supervision, and an assistant works under a radiographer's personal supervision. A company licensed in Texas that sends a crew to a Louisiana turnaround files for reciprocity first.

That licensing covers radiation safety, not image quality. A Gulf Coast radiographer normally carries both the radiographer certification the state recognizes and the employer's SNT-TC-1A RT certification for technique and interpretation, and an RT course on its own licenses nobody. Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States; our RT course prepares you for the employer's technique and interpretation examinations.

Choosing NDT training on the Gulf Coast

The right route depends less on the provider than on where you stand today.

  • No NDT employer yet. A full-time school with labs gives you hands-on hours before your first job and a structured start, but it means time out of paid work.
  • Hired as a helper. Contractors on the channel and in the river parishes take on helpers and trainees, then arrange formal training while the experience hours build. Ask early how those hours will be delivered and who signs the records.
  • Already certified and adding a method. Self-paced online theory with the practical at your employer is usually the quickest way to add UT to MT and PT, or RT to UT, without losing shifts.
  • Moving from the crafts. Welders, pipefitters and boilermakers already read drawings and know weld defects, which makes VT and the welding-inspection route natural first steps.

Before paying anyone, ask four things. Will the hours satisfy the written practice of the company you work for or want to join? Who examines your practical, on which specimens? What records will you leave with? And does the provider claim to certify you, which under SNT-TC-1A only an employer can do? The NDT training overview and the training FAQ set out how Atlantis answers each one.

Qualifying a crew across several Gulf Coast plants

Turnaround season exposes weak programmes: a contractor with crews at Baytown, Lake Charles and Corpus Christi finds out on the first day of an outage whether every technician's file matches the written practice the operator audited. The fix is one written practice for the whole company and one training route behind it. Theory goes online so night-shift and rotation workers can finish it between hitches.

The practical end is delivered on site. An ASNT NDT Level III holding UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, with over 11 years in the field, trains and examines at your shop or yard on your equipment, procedures and representative parts, so examinations reflect the plant work your crews perform. Every technician leaves with hours, experience, examination grades and vision records filed to your written practice, ready for the next operator audit. Describe your sites, methods and head-count on the crew training enquiry. We reply within one business day.

Practise before your practical

Practical examinations on the coast tend to be plant-shaped: thickness readings on corroded pipe, weld scans on piping, indications to size and record. Practical NDT puts that procedure in a 3D simulator you can run in a browser, on a PC or in VR, with a twelve-step workflow in which credit goes only to what you record. The storage-tank and heat-exchanger workplaces mirror terminal and plant jobs, and the MT simulator suits shipyard and fabrication candidates. The simulator rehearses the steps; supervised hours, the practical examination and the employer's certification still have to happen for real.

The free NDT practice tests cover the written general and specific examinations at Level II.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training on the Gulf Coast

How long does it take to get NDT certified on the Gulf Coast?

It depends on the training and experience hours in your employer's written practice, which follow the SNT-TC-1A recommendations for each method and level. Theory moves at your pace; the supervised experience hours take longer, and the hours planner shows both.

Can I take NDT training online in Texas or Louisiana?

The theory, yes, from anywhere with an internet connection. The hands-on training and practical examination are done in person at the employer's facility. More on online NDT training.

Is there NDT training near me in Houston?

Atlantis has an office in Houston but no classroom, so there is no walk-in course to attend. Individuals study online and complete practicals with their employer; companies get training delivered at their own facility.

Which method should I start with for refinery work?

UT, because thickness readings drive plant inspection programmes, usually alongside VT. If you join a shipyard or fabrication shop instead, MT and PT come first.

Will my certification carry over to a contractor in Louisiana?

No certification under SNT-TC-1A carries over automatically, because each employer issues its own. Your records do carry over, and they let the new contractor recertify you with less repetition. Crossing from Texas into Louisiana makes no difference to that.

Do I need an API 510, 570 or 653 certificate to work in NDT?

No. Those are inspector certifications issued by API for people who run in-service inspection programmes; NDT technicians are certified by method under the employer's written practice.

How do I become an NDT Level III?

Most candidates pass the ASNT Basic and method examinations and are then certified by their employer. ASNT Level III training prepares you for those examinations at your own pace.

Can I prepare for the AWS CWI exam on the Gulf Coast?

Yes. The six-day AWS CWI exam prep runs as corporate training at your facility, online, or one-to-one online or in person; AWS administers the examination and certifies. City pages cover Houston, Baton Rouge, Beaumont, Lake Charles and Mobile.
